title: IR-Runbook-Credential-Theft
summary: Original summary of current LSASS credential dumping response, with a clearly marked superseded legacy conflict.
content:
## 3.1 [Immediate] Isolate the affected host
Disconnect the endpoint from wired, wireless, VPN, and other network segments immediately. The archived Legacy-IR-Playbook-2024 v1.4 (Mar 2, 2024) says to isolate within 30 minutes and power down; that conflicting advice is superseded. Isolate now and preserve the running system for evidence.

## 3.2 [Immediate] Do not reboot; capture volatile memory
Keep the host powered on. Acquire volatile memory with approved live-response tooling before terminating processes or rebooting, because rebooting destroys in-memory LSASS evidence.

## 4.1 [Investigate] Pull Windows and Sysmon Event ID 10 (citation: Threat-Intel-2025-14 p.4)
Review the preceding 24 hours of process-access events targeting lsass.exe. Record the source process, user, target PID, and granted access mask. Cross-reference the collection and indicators with Threat-Intel-2025-14 p.4.

## 4.2 [Investigate] Check suspicious LSASS access and credential-dumping tool signatures (citation: Threat-Intel-2025-14 p.6)
Compare process hashes and loaded modules against approved threat-intelligence signatures, including Mimikatz, ProcDump, Nanodump, and comsvcs.dll. Check signature context against Threat-Intel-2025-14 p.6.

## 5.1 [Recover] Rotate exposed credentials
Reset passwords for accounts active or cached on the host during the exposure window, revoke active sessions, and invalidate relevant Kerberos tickets. Escalate a KRBTGT reset when domain-controller exposure is confirmed.
